catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adrian-of-cas: A 1913 entry on Adrian of Castello — the Italian cardinal of stormy fortunes. Thomas Walsh follows his rise and falls. Corneto's bishop played for high stakes. Popes made and unmade him. A Renaissance prelate's checkered life. His letters reveal the curia's secrets.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ancient-see-o: A 1913 entry on the ancient see of Oslo — Norway's eastern bishopric. Arthur Taylor gives its Catholic past. Its bishops served the medieval town. The old cathedral's ruins remain. A vanished see of the north. Its ruins lie beneath the modern streets.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antonio-and-p: This 1913 reference piece on the Pollaiuolo brothers — Antonio and Piero, Florence's craftsmen. Gaston Sortais praises their bronze and paint. Their papal tombs guard St. Peter's. Strength marks their every figure. The workshop of the Renaissance. Their Hercules bronzes guard the museums.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bartolome-est: A 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Murillo — the sweet painter of Seville. Louis Gillet honors his Immaculates. His beggar boys charm the museums. The Andalusian heaven glows in his blues. The most beloved Spanish painter. His Prodigal Son hangs in Dublin.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-benedetto-mar: This 1913 reference piece on Benedetto Marcello — the composer of the psalms. William Finn honors his Estro poetico. His fifty psalms sing David's words. Venice's palaces heard his music. The noble dilettante of the baroque. His satire mocked the opera stage.
